name: Skip a stone five or more times
blurb: A physics problem you can solve on any beach: the right stone, roughly a 20-degree angle, plenty of spin, and a low fast throw.
steps: Select properly: flat, smooth, palm-sized and reasonably heavy. Stone selection is half the skill.
Grip with the index finger hooked around the edge and the thumb on top, which is what lets you impart spin.
Crouch low so the release is close to the water, and throw sidearm rather than overhand.
Release at about 20 degrees to the water — the angle matters more than the speed.
Snap the wrist hard on release. Spin is what stabilises the stone across bounces.
Adjust one variable at a time until you find the combination that works on that water.
tips: Too steep an angle and it dives on the first bounce; too flat and it just skids and stops.
Choppy water makes it nearly impossible. Wait for calm.
proof: Five or more skips, repeatably, on calm water.
